quote_zh: 向反应釜中加入200mLDMF、11.8g 2-四氢呋喃甲醇(99％，0.115mol)和8.6g氢氧化钾(85％，0.13mol)，开动搅拌，控制釜温在5℃
arithmetic_check: Closes within the precision of the printed figures. Stated inputs: 200 mL DMF; 11.8 g 2-tetrahydrofuran methanol at 99 percent, 0.115 mol; 8.6 g potassium hydroxide at 85 percent, 0.13 mol; benzoate salt at 98.2 percent, 0.1 mol, no mass printed. Stated output: 32.6 g of product at 95.9 percent HPLC content, two-step yield 89.8 percent on the methyl ester. Checks: 11.8 x 0.99 = 11.68 g at 102.13 gives 0.1144 mol against 0.115 mol printed, within 0.6 percent. 8.6 x 0.85 = 7.31 g at 56.11 gives 0.1303 mol against 0.13 mol printed, within 0.3 percent, so the potassium hydroxide mass and strength do imply its own molecular weight. Product 32.6 x 0.959 = 31.26 g at 348.80 gives 0.0896 mol, which is 89.6 percent of the 0.1 mol of salt charged, against 89.8 percent printed; taking the printed mass and content at the top of their rounding, 32.649 x 0.9594 = 31.32 g, gives 0.0898 mol and reproduces 89.8 percent exactly, so the 0.2 point residual is rounding. Theoretical maximum on 0.1 mol is 34.88 g, above the 32.6 g printed. So no mass_balance_implausible and no molar_mass_inconsistent. THE ONE DISCREPANCY: the 89.8 percent that the arithmetic reproduces as a single-step yield on the 0.1 mol charged here is printed as a two-step yield calculated on the methyl ester of step (1). Both readings can only be true together if step (1) were quantitative at exactly 0.1 mol of methyl ester, and step (1) prints no charge in this section, so the stated basis is unverifiable here. Recorded as printed, flagged cross_reference_unresolved, not corrected. For the same reason step (1)'s output charge is absent and scale_discontinuity could not be tested either way.
